idiom_name: static Create/Open factory method on the aggregate + private constructor (standalone factory class when creation needs repositories)
implementation_notes: C# can only hide construction by making the constructor private or protected, so the idiomatic DDD factory is a public static method with a domain name that guards its arguments (ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull, ArgumentOutOfRangeException) and returns a fully valid instance, while record types with primary constructors cover value-shaped products. What replaces the classic factory class is the static factory method on the aggregate itself; keep a constructor-injected IOrderFactory when creation must load other aggregates or be swapped in tests, and note that asynchronous creation cannot live in a constructor at all.
pitfalls: A public constructor left beside the factory re-opens the bypass; when a serialiser or ORM needs one, keep it private and mark it infrastructure-only.
Records generate a public primary constructor and a with expression that can replace any property, so an invariant-bearing record is only as safe as the validating constructor it exposes.
Creation that awaits a repository cannot happen in a constructor; put it on the standalone factory and return Task<Order>.
